:::{#rem-angle-unit-circle-angle}
#### How the two angles relate

For vectors in the plane, the [angle between two vectors](#def-angle)
equals the [angle on the unit circle](algebra-trigonometry.qmd#def-angle-unit-circle)
between the points in their directions.
The point in the direction of a nonzero vector, $\vecf{x}$, is $\vecf{x} / \norm{\vecf{x}}$.
So the [cosine similarity](#def-cosine-similarity) of two vectors
is the [dot product](linear-algebra.qmd#def-dot-product) of their points.
Rotating the plane puts the first point at $(1, 0)$,
with no change to the distance between the points along the circle or to their dot product.
For the angle on the unit circle, $\angpar$, the second point is then $(\cos\angpar, \pm\sin\angpar)$,
so the dot product of the points is $\cos\angpar$.
Applying $\arccos$ to it returns $\angpar$, which lies in $[0, \pi]$.

:::
